name: Postmodernism
summary: Postmodernism is a late-20th-century philosophical and cultural movement that doubts the grand narratives of modernity, such as progress through reason, Marxist emancipation or religious history, and the claim that knowledge can stand outside language and power. Its thinkers trace how truth, identity and norms are produced by discourse and institutions, and they favor difference, local narratives and dissent over universal consensus. Politically it was taken up mainly on the academic left, in feminism, queer theory, multiculturalism and postcolonial thought.
scope: French post-structuralist and postmodern philosophy of roughly 1968-1995: Lyotard's The Postmodern Condition, Foucault's work on power/knowledge, discipline and sexuality, Derrida's deconstruction and Specters of Marx, with Baudrillard and Deleuze as context, and the political uses of these ideas in postmodern feminism and postcolonial thought. Because it is a philosophy rather than a political program, answers follow the political implications usually drawn by its scholars and academic adherents, and many are low confidence. Postmodernism in art and architecture, Rorty's pragmatism and the Marxist critique of postmodernism (Jameson) are excluded.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Lyotard describes the commodification of knowledge under performativity critically, and Derrida lists the contradictions of the free market among the plagues of post-1989 capitalism.

public-ownership.rationale: Postmodernists criticize capitalism but are equally suspicious of state power and of the Marxist programs that called for nationalization, so no clear answer follows.

property-fundamental.rationale: Postmodernism treats rights claims as historically constructed rather than natural, and its thinkers criticize capitalist property relations, so an absolute property right is rejected.

worker-ownership.rationale: Some adherents sympathize with self-management, but postmodernism offers no economic program and distrusts emancipatory blueprints of this kind.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Foucault's analysis of the panopticon and disciplinary power treats surveillance as a central technique of domination, and this critique is one of the most widely adopted parts of postmodern thought.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents' attention to how discourse produces marginalization pulls toward restriction, but their suspicion of state and legal power over discourse pulls the other way.

strong-leader.rationale: Postmodernism is a critique of centralized and totalizing power; a leader who overrides institutions concentrates exactly the authority it distrusts.

state-harmful.rationale: Foucault moves analysis away from the state toward diffuse power, and Derrida calls for a critique of the state, but neither calls for abolishing it; adherents are split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: Foucault treats police, prisons and similar institutions as instruments of class power whose hidden violence should be exposed and fought, a view central to his political work.

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

decide-locally.rationale: Lyotard favors local, heterogeneous language games over universal frameworks; adherents carry this into a preference for local over central authority, though the texts do not discuss administrative levels.

rehabilitation.rationale: Foucault argues the reforming, 'correctional' prison is itself the disciplinary technique that produces delinquency, so adherents reject punishment and rehabilitation alike as framed here.

traditional-family.rationale: Foucault names the family among institutions that maintain class power, and postmodern feminism seeks to destabilize patriarchal norms.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Foucault's history of sexuality underpins queer theory and opposes heteronormativity, though some queer theorists criticize marriage itself as a normalizing institution.

more-religion-public.rationale: Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives explicitly includes Christianity among the grand narratives that no longer legitimate knowledge or society.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Postmodernism became closely linked with multiculturalism, postcolonial thought and legal scholarship that emphasizes racial inequality.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Postmodern feminism, building on Foucault through Judith Butler, rejects a universal female subject and treats gender as produced by discourse and power.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Postmodernists treat national identities as constructed and, in Derrida's words, mythic, and they favor heterogeneity over a protected national tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: Postmodernism distrusts both revolutionary grand narratives and the institutions it seeks to destabilize; deference to established institutions sits worse with it than gradualism does.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Derrida lists the deportation of immigrants and the building of new walls among the ten plagues of the new world order.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Derrida criticizes international law as applied hypocritically against weaker nations yet calls for a transformed international order, so adherents give no clear answer.

nation-first.rationale: Derrida's New International unites those who criticize the state and national concepts, and postmodernists reject national identity as a grounding value.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents distrust universalist human-rights justifications and international law that is applied selectively, though some, including Derrida, did not rule intervention out.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Rejecting the Enlightenment narrative of progress through reason and science is central to postmodernism, and Lyotard treats technology as serving performativity rather than emancipation.

revolution-justified.rationale: Foucault in 1971 accepted the proletariat's violent struggle for power, but postmodernists generally reject the revolutionary grand narrative, so support is qualified.

experts-over-public.rationale: The power/knowledge critique of medicine, psychiatry and expert 'decision makers' is central to the tradition, which treats expert authority as a form of power rather than neutral knowledge.

central-planning.rationale: Postmodernists reject totalizing systems and the Marxist grand narrative that underwrote central planning.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Derrida treats the clash of protectionism and free trade as a contradiction of the market rather than taking a side.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Postmodernists reject utopian end-states of history such as the communist abolition of money as grand narratives, though they criticize commodification.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Lyotard criticizes systems models that integrate all social actors into one performative whole, and the postmodern preference for dissensus over consensus counts against state-organized class collaboration.

one-party-rule.rationale: Incredulity toward metanarratives such as Marxism is the defining postmodern stance, and many of its founders broke with the French Communist Party; rule by a party with the correct ideology is what it rejects.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Foucault urged political theory to 'cut off the head of the king', and postmodernists reject inherited authority as natural.

democracy-best.rationale: Postmodernists criticize liberal democracy as claiming to have realized history's end, but Derrida and Rorty still affirm a democracy to come or liberal democracy over alternatives.

workers-councils.rationale: Council communism rests on the class-based grand narrative postmodernists abandoned.

right-to-secede.rationale: Postmodernists value local difference but also treat national and ethnic identities as mythic constructions, so they give no clear answer on secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Foucault treats human nature as a construct formed within a civilization that serves class power, so claims of natural fitness to rule are what genealogy unmasks.

political-violence-never.rationale: Foucault argued that the proletariat's struggle could involve violence and that 'one makes war to win, not because it is just'.

war-builds-character.rationale: Foucault's account of biopower links modern states to industrial warfare that kills millions, and Derrida treats inter-ethnic and economic wars as plagues.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Scripture as a source of law is a paradigm grand narrative, which postmodernism holds can no longer legitimate social order.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Postmodernism is tied to multiculturalism and postcolonial thought and treats ethnic national identity as a myth; Derrida names inter-ethnic wars driven by it as a plague.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Postmodernists reject Marxism's historical narrative; Foucault's genealogy stresses contingency and replaces ideology with power/knowledge, though he still spoke in class terms in 1971.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Adherents oppose inequality but distrust any single universal standard of equality, favoring heterogeneity; the tradition gives no clear answer.

civilizational-union.rationale: Postmodernism rejects totalizing identities and grand narratives such as religion or civilization as foundations of political order.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Postmodernists tend to treat 'nature' as a discursive construct, which cuts against intrinsic value, while some ecological strands affirm it; adherents are split.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Postmodernism criticizes modernity's progress narrative but does not reject industrial society or wish to return to an earlier one.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Some strands (Deleuze and Guattari's de-territorializing flows) were later read as accelerationist, while Lyotard is wary of technology serving performativity; adherents are split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Lyotard describes the handing of regulation to machines and performativity criteria critically, as a threat to the legitimation of knowledge and justice.

restore-past-order.rationale: Postmodernism rejects narratives of a lost origin or presence as much as narratives of progress, and Foucault's genealogy shows past orders were contingent rather than natural.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Its adherents lean left but reject the Marxist story of a future communist society, so they are split on this ultimate goal.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Derrida keeps a 'spirit' of Marx's critique while the movement broke with Marxist class theory, so adherents are split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Postmodernism broke with Communism and rejects any single class or party claiming total authority.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Derrida ties wars and the arms trade to the new world order, but the movement rejects inevitable laws of history, so 'inevitably' cuts against it.

state-as-business.rationale: Lyotard criticizes the rule of performativity and efficiency and Foucault analyzes neoliberal governmentality critically.

media-academia-power.rationale: Foucault locates power in discourses and institutions such as schools, medicine and knowledge production rather than in sovereign office-holders; an inference to this framing.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Postmodern thought treats identities and categories such as race as produced by discourse and power, not by biology.

total-state.rationale: Postmodernism rejects totalizing systems, and Foucault's work is a critique of state and institutional control over life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Postmodern thinkers treat national myths of decline and renewal as grand narratives to be doubted.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Its political uses in postcolonial thought are critiques of imperial expansion.

universal-morality.rationale: Postmodernism is defined by its rejection of universal, foundational truths and grand narratives in favor of local, plural ones.

single-common-good.rationale: Lyotard rejects consensus as a goal and favors dissent and plural language games over one rational answer.

revive-national-language.rationale: Postcolonial strands value reclaiming suppressed languages, but the movement distrusts national identity projects, so adherents are split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Lyotard and Foucault attack the Enlightenment claim that reason is a neutral, universal guide, treating it as a discourse bound up with power and one narrative among many.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Postmodern feminism and queer theory treat gender roles as products of discourse and power and oppose laws that fix them.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Multiculturalism and postcolonial thought, which adopted these ideas, oppose racial classification, and Foucault treats classification as a technique of power.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Foucault, in debate with Chomsky, said institutions like courts serve class power, though he held that power is diffuse rather than held by one class.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Postmodern thought defends difference and local narratives against a single dominant culture, so it rejects demands that minorities give up their own.

elite-replacement.rationale: It treats power as diffuse and produced by discourse, not directed by a hidden plan, and it favors the multicultural left that rejects replacement claims.

national-mission.rationale: It rejects grand narratives of progress and universal political systems, and postcolonial uses reject exporting one nation’s system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Postmodern feminism and Foucault’s analyses of power treat gender hierarchy as built into institutions and discourse.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: It analyzes power as pervasive rather than the moral failing of individuals, so adherents are split on corrupt, out-of-touch elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Foucault’s work on biopower and the normalizing disciplines criticizes state control of reproduction and eugenics.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Postmodern feminism, multiculturalism and postcolonial thought, which took up these ideas, press for equal rights for excluded groups, though Lyotard and Foucault distrust universal claims; the rights claim is usually drawn by scholars as an implication.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Postmodern thought distrusts universal norms, which cuts against a common code, but also distrusts religious authority; its adherents are split and the texts do not address it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Postmodernism doubts the grand narrative of the social contract and shows how consent is manufactured by power; adherents split between valuing dissent and distrusting consent.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The inseparability of knowledge and power is a founding claim of Lyotard and Foucault.

separated-powers.rationale: Foucault stresses that power is diffuse throughout society, not located in state branches, so dividing state power is of limited interest; adherents are split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The ideology says little about term limits, and its distrust of power points both ways; adherents are split or indifferent.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Postmodernism rejects universal hierarchies of value and favors difference and local narratives over a single standard of progress.

death-penalty.rationale: Foucault's Discipline and Punish criticized the penal system and spectacle of punishment, and postmodern thinkers like Derrida opposed the death penalty.

minority-language-support.rationale: Its defense of difference and local narratives, and its use in multiculturalism and postcolonial thought, supports minority languages.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Foucault and the postmodern emphasis on dissent, difference and the critique of normalization favor eccentric ways of living.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Adherents split: the movement distrusts consensus and founding narratives but favors dissent and plural voices; it has no position on constitution-making.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Foucault criticised the church's pastoral power but equally distrusted state power, so adherents are split.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Foucault's analysis treats sovereign, sacral power as a historical form of domination to be questioned, and divine legitimation is a grand narrative the movement doubts.

character-from-environment.rationale: Foucault in the 1971 debate with Chomsky doubted a fixed human nature and treated subjects as produced by discourse, institutions and power.

equal-parenting.rationale: Postmodern feminists were split between criticising gender norms in custody law and doubting rights presumptions; no stated position.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Postmodern thinkers reject grand narratives and Eurocentric history, and postcolonial uses favour plural, decentred accounts.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Postcolonial thought drawn from postmodernism rejects civilizing missions as discourses that legitimate domination.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Lyotard sees capitalism absorbing challenges while Derrida's Specters lists the new order's plagues; adherents are split on this.

animal-use-humane.rationale: No settled position; Derrida's animal writing criticized industrial animal use while the movement as a whole is silent.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Foucault held that power runs through all social relations, so withdrawal is not neutral, and his and Derrida's work is politically engaged.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Baudrillard and Lyotard describe media and commodified knowledge as reproducing the order; the claim is less central for other postmodernists.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Postcolonial strands accept something like it, but postmodernists distrust the Marxist grand narrative of structural exploitation, so they are split.

party-own-road.rationale: Postmodernists broke with party-based communism and reject its metanarrative, so the question has little purchase.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Postcolonial strands may sympathize, but the movement does not endorse group leadership by descent and is split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Lyotard and Foucault criticized both Soviet communism and Western institutions, but the equivalence thesis is not theirs and the academic left is split on it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Postmodernists question official memory and monuments, yet favour keeping contested memory visible; adherents are split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.

reviewHistory.rationale: Postmodern theory favors dissent and plural local voices but offers no settled view on how representation should work.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

democratic-peace.rationale: It doubts universal narratives of progress, including that one regime type brings peace.

non-intervention.rationale: Postcolonial uses are wary of intervention, though Foucault himself backed some humanitarian action, so the 'any reason' wording is tentative.

industrial-unions.rationale: The ideology is indifferent to union structure.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Foucault's history of sexuality and queer theory question state regulation of intimate life.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Lyotard's report argues the public should have free access to memory and data banks.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Foucault's history of sexuality treats such norms as products of disciplinary power, and queer theory grew from this work.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Postmodern thought favours dissent and local narratives over enforced consensus, and Foucault was an activist against state repression.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: It broke with Marxist grand narratives but its academic adherents remained largely on the left; adherents are split.

alienated-labor.rationale: Lyotard and others reject the Marxist grand narrative that frames alienation, while Derrida keeps parts of Marx; adherents are split.

property-franchise.rationale: Foucault and later thinkers on the academic left support inclusion and attack exclusion of groups from political life.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Postmodern feminism links patriarchal domination of women to wider hierarchies, and ecofeminist thought extends this to nature.

reification.rationale: Derrida's Specters of Marx treats Marx's critique of capital as still valuable, though postmodernists distrust Marx's grand narrative.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Foucault's power/knowledge claim treats freedoms as shaped by institutions and wealth, and the academic left draws this conclusion.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Foucault shows how legal forms hide power, while many adherents still defend the rule of law; the sources leave it split.

racial-franchise.rationale: Postmodernism favours difference and the inclusion of marginal groups and opposes ethnic exclusion, as noted in postcolonial and multiculturalist uses.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Postmodernism's support for difference, multiculturalism and minority rights runs against religious marriage restrictions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a minority faith contradicts the pluralism and defence of minorities that are central to postmodern politics.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Foucault's work on sexuality criticizes norms that classify and exclude sexual minorities, and the tradition fed queer theory.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Foucault's Discipline and Punish treats prisons and policing as instruments of disciplinary power, and he helped found a prison-information group.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Foucault's work treats disciplinary drill of bodies as a technique of power, so regimented youth organizations are a target of critique.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Rejecting grand narratives, including nationalist origin stories, is central; Lyotard's account of narratives is stated in The Postmodern Condition.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Foucault's History of Sexuality treats sex as produced by discourse and power, and Butler-style postmodern feminism extends this to sex.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Derrida's Specters of Marx keeps a Marxist spirit but the movement doubts universal emancipation narratives, so it is split.

person-over-state.rationale: Foucault and others critique the humanist subject, so a person-centred framing is not clearly endorsed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Adherents are split: postcolonial thought backs minority group politics while the movement also doubts fixed identities.

racial-pride.rationale: Adherents are split: it backs minority and postcolonial pride but distrusts essentialised identities.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Postcolonial thought, a main political use of these ideas, favours reworking global economic relations, though the main thinkers do not discuss rules specifically.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Postcolonial thought, a main political use of these ideas, analyses domination within and between societies; internal colonialism is not specifically discussed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: In the Chomsky debate Foucault doubts that human nature is a useful or fixed scientific concept and that rights should be grounded in it.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Derrida and Lyotard criticize liberal consensus and post-1989 triumphalism, and treat democracy as an open promise rather than a set of procedures, so they would not accept the procedural definition alone.

premarital-sex.rationale: Foucault's History of Sexuality treats sexual norms as products of power and discourse rather than natural law, so an adherent would not hold women to a separate moral standard.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Adherents are split: the left reception favors redistribution, while Foucault's critique of the welfare apparatus as discipline makes them wary of administered schemes.

race-social-construct.rationale: Treating identity categories as produced by discourse and institutions is central to the movement, and its uptake in multiculturalism and postcolonial thought applies this to race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Postmodern feminism supports equality aims but Foucault's work on governmentality makes many wary of state bodies managing identities; adherents are genuinely divided.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Lyotard's incredulity toward grand narratives, religious history included, rules out a single literal authoritative reading of scripture.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Postmodern thinkers rarely address territorial disputes, and local voting both respects local narratives and relies on universal procedure; adherents are split.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Foucault's work on discipline and punishment criticises state violence and institutions that claim authority over deviants.

self-ownership.rationale: Foucault and others hold that the subject is produced by discourse and power rather than being a pre-given owner of itself.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Lyotard's incredulity toward metanarratives rejects returning to a unifying tradition as an answer to modernity.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Split: Lyotard warns that computerised knowledge becomes commodified, while the academic left often favours less work; the sources take no stand.

police-more-powers.rationale: Foucault treats police, prisons and similar institutions as instruments of class power whose hidden violence should be exposed and fought, a view central to his political work. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

missingStatements.text: Claims to objective knowledge are shaped by the interests of those in power.
missingStatements.rationale: The inseparability of knowledge and power is a founding claim of Lyotard and Foucault and the core of the postmodern critique.

missingStatements.text: There are universal truths about morality and society that hold across all cultures.
missingStatements.rationale: Postmodernism is defined by its rejection of universal, foundational truths and grand narratives in favor of local, plural ones.

notes: Postmodern thinkers rarely stated policy positions, so most economic and many social answers are inferred from the left politics of the movement's academic adherents and marked low. Foucault's views shifted (more Marxist in 1971, closer to ethics and interest in liberalism late in life), and Rorty's 'postmodernist bourgeois liberalism' would answer several governance questions more favorably to liberal democracy and markets. Critics such as Habermas and Chomsky charge the tradition with relativism; adherents dispute that label.
